passage:
Yogesh had stopped opening the banking app. Two months earlier a colleague's hot tip had swallowed most of his emergency savings, and each time the balance flashed he felt stupid enough to want to vanish. At home he changed the subject whenever his parents asked about money.

On Sunday his friend Dhruv found him staring at a spreadsheet he had built and deleted twice. "You look terrible."

After a long pause Yogesh told him everything. Dhruv didn't laugh. "People lose money on tips all the time. Can we write down what happened?"

They made a list: bought after one message, no research, put in more to win it back. Yogesh set two rules: never put in money he couldn't afford to lose, and never act on someone else's excitement. Then he opened the app, started a small monthly transfer, and rang his mother.

qa.q: What two rules did Yogesh set?
qa.a: Yogesh set two rules: never put in money he couldn't afford to lose, and never act on someone else's excitement.

qa.q: Why had Yogesh stopped opening the banking app?
qa.a: Each time the balance flashed he felt stupid enough to want to vanish, so avoiding the app was a way of hiding the shame.

qa.q: What would you advise Yogesh to do now that he has told Dhruv?
qa.a: Keep reviewing what happened, stick to the rules, rebuild slowly with the small monthly transfer, and keep his family in the picture.

qa.q: How does Dhruv see Yogesh's loss?
qa.a: Dhruv treats it as a common experience rather than something to laugh at, and helps Yogesh look at what happened calmly.

grounding: Yogesh loses savings on a hot tip, feels stupid and hides it, then stops, reviews, tells someone and rebuilds slowly with rules.
